title: Freezing exposure after cherry bloom had no clear period change at Liestal and Washington in 1951–2025
abstract: We compared freezing exposure near cherry bloom in 1951–1987 and 1988–2025. We used fixed annual bloom records and quality-approved GHCN daily minimum temperatures. In 14-day windows from observed bloom, freezing-year fractions changed by +3.6 percentage points at Liestal and +7.6 points at Washington. Both 95% block bootstrap intervals included zero. At Liestal, fixed-date freezing exposure decreased by 33.3 points while exposure from observed bloom did not. Washington airport did not show the same clear fixed-date decrease. The evidence did not establish a common timing mechanism across the two regions. Kyoto had too few complete later windows for a test. Two Washington stations gave very different exposure rates in the same years. Station choice, missing weather, different bloom rules, and sparse events limit inference. We measured temperature exposure, not frost damage, air pollution, or biodiversity loss. The package includes code, data hashes, derived exposures, coverage audits, and reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Freezing-window period changes at two sites. Individual 95% block bootstrap intervals include zero for observed-bloom exposure.
